stem:
Falguni wants a circular hole of radius $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the centre of a square sheet of side $14\,\mathrm{cm}$. She will use a compass.

Which claim correctly states where the compass point must be placed and what radius is needed?

options.text: Place the compass point at the centre of the square and open the compass to radius $4\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Place the compass point at a corner of the square and open it to $14\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Place the compass point anywhere on the sheet; only the $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ opening matters.
Draw the hole freehand, because neat artwork on the square sheet is enough.

teacher.key_rationale: A compass arc needs the chosen centre and radius: centre of the square and 4 cm. A corner with side length swaps surface numbers. Anywhere omits the centre. Freehand swaps the compass mechanism.
